\end{aligned}

def compile_circuit(function: QuantumCircuit):
    # Compiles a circuit for use in the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm.

    n = function.num_qubits - 1
    qc = QuantumCircuit(n + 1, n)
    qc.x(n)
    qc.h(range(n + 1))
    qc.compose(function, inplace=True)
    qc.h(range(n))
    qc.measure(range(n), range(n))
    return qc

def bv_algorithm(function: QuantumCircuit):
    qc = compile_circuit(function)
    result = AerSimulator().run(qc, shots=1, memory=True).result()
    return result.get_memory()[0]

known_boundaries: Historical plan note: Earlier G1 pilot reportedly rejected unqualified bound ket inside set sum while explicit dimension2 passed; retain original failure and label any dimension annotation as authored adaptation. No claim that these BV literals fail before executing them.
Historical plan note: Do not treat f(x) as an implicitly declared Boolean function; ordinary implicit multiplication is not this source semantics.
Historical plan note: Literal binary dot product and XOR meanings require declared domains; generic scalar dot/product semantics cannot be substituted silently.
Historical plan note: All16 secrets at fixed n4 are a finite family, not arbitrary n or whole source.
Historical plan note: No worker/build/GUI/SDK calls occur in this plan. Notebook-lane samehash seeded executions remain separate.

shared_requests.adaptation: Bind n4; expand16source sum terms; integer basis labels with disclosed dimension16; preserve minus ancilla.

limits: Some expanded XOR/dot requests may hit existing input/parser complexity budgets. Preserve exact rejected inputs; a grouped equivalent sum is a disclosed follow-up, not silent replacement. Native expression failures cannot be inferred before execution.
